quests.sentence: She said that she was tired.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was tired shifts the original present tense 'am tired' back one step into the past, following that, since the reporting itself happened in the past.
quests.nativeTip: When reporting speech, present tense in the original shifts back to past tense.

quests.sentence: He said that he liked the restaurant.
quests.ruleExplanation: Liked shifts the original present tense 'like' back into the past, with he replacing the original I as the reporting subject.
quests.nativeTip: The verb shifts back to past tense the same way, right after that and the new subject.

quests.sentence: They said that they needed more time.
quests.ruleExplanation: Needed shifts the original present tense 'need' back into the past, with they replacing the original we.
quests.nativeTip: The same present-to-past shift applies to a plural subject's original statement.

quests.sentence: She said that she had finished the project.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had finished shifts the original simple past 'finished' back one more step into the past perfect, since the original statement was already in the past.
quests.nativeTip: A simple past verb in the original statement shifts back further, into the past perfect.

quests.sentence: They said that they had seen the movie.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had seen shifts the original simple past 'saw' back into the past perfect, following the reported-speech backshift rule.
quests.nativeTip: The same past-to-past-perfect shift applies to a plural subject's original statement.

quests.sentence: She said that he had left early.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had left shifts the original 'left' into the past perfect, and he replaces the speaker's original I, since a different person is now reporting it.
quests.nativeTip: Pronouns shift too — he replaces the original I, alongside the tense backshift.

quests.sentence: He said that he would call me.
quests.ruleExplanation: Would call shifts the original modal will back to would, with me replacing the original you.
quests.nativeTip: Will shifts back to would in reported speech, the modal's past-tense counterpart.

quests.sentence: They said that they could help us.
quests.ruleExplanation: Could help shifts the original modal can back to could, with us replacing the original you.
quests.nativeTip: Can shifts back to could the same way, right after that and the new subject.

quests.sentence: She said that she had to leave immediately.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had to leave shifts the original modal must to had to, a common but slightly irregular modal shift in reported speech.
quests.nativeTip: Must often shifts to had to in reported speech, a less obvious modal pairing.

quests.sentence: He said that he would see me the next day.
quests.ruleExplanation: The next day replaces the original tomorrow, since the reporting now happens on a different day than when the words were first spoken.
quests.nativeTip: Time words shift too — tomorrow becomes the next day when reporting speech from a different day.

quests.sentence: She said that she was there then.
quests.ruleExplanation: There replaces here and then replaces now, since the speaker is no longer in that original place or moment when reporting it later.
quests.nativeTip: Place and time words shift together — here becomes there, and now becomes then.

quests.sentence: They said they would finish it that day.
quests.ruleExplanation: That day replaces the original today, and it replaces this, since the reporting happens away from that original moment.
quests.nativeTip: Today shifts to that day, and this shifts to it, when reporting speech later or elsewhere.

quests.sentence: She told him to close the door.
quests.ruleExplanation: Told him to close converts the original command Close the door into an object-plus-infinitive structure, with him as the person being told.
quests.nativeTip: A reported command uses object plus to plus the base verb, not the original imperative form.

quests.sentence: He asked us to wait outside.
quests.ruleExplanation: Asked us to wait converts the original request Please wait outside into an object-plus-infinitive structure.
quests.nativeTip: Asked works the same way for a polite request, using object plus infinitive.

quests.sentence: She told them not to touch it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Not to touch adds not before the infinitive, converting the original negative command Don't touch that into the reported form.
quests.nativeTip: A negative command adds not before to, right between the object and the infinitive.

quests.sentence: She asked if I was coming.
quests.ruleExplanation: If I was coming uses statement word order (subject before verb), unlike the original direct question Are you coming?, which had inverted word order.
quests.nativeTip: A reported yes/no question uses if, then normal statement word order — no inversion, unlike a direct question.

quests.sentence: He asked whether I had finished the assignment.
quests.ruleExplanation: Whether I had finished uses statement word order, converting the original inverted question Did you finish the report? into a normal clause.
quests.nativeTip: Whether works like if here, still followed by statement word order, not question order.

quests.sentence: They asked if I could help them.
quests.ruleExplanation: If I could help uses statement word order, converting the original inverted question Can you help me? into a normal clause.
quests.nativeTip: If plus statement word order applies here too, even with a modal in the original question.

quests.sentence: She asked where I lived.
quests.ruleExplanation: Where I lived uses statement word order after the question word where, unlike the original inverted Where do you live?
quests.nativeTip: A reported WH question keeps the question word but drops the inversion — statement word order follows.

quests.sentence: He asked what time the meeting started.
quests.ruleExplanation: What time the meeting started drops the auxiliary does entirely and uses plain statement order, unlike the original What time does the meeting start?
quests.nativeTip: The question word leads, then statement order follows, with no do/does needed.

quests.sentence: They asked why I had left.
quests.ruleExplanation: Why I had left uses statement order and shifts the original did leave back to had left, following both reported-speech rules at once.
quests.nativeTip: Why still leads the reported question, followed by statement word order and a backshifted verb.

quests.sentence: Could you tell me where the station is?
quests.ruleExplanation: Where the station is uses statement word order after the polite frame, rather than the inverted Where is the station? you'd expect in a direct question.
quests.nativeTip: A polite question frame like could you tell me is followed by statement word order, not inverted question order.

quests.sentence: Do you know what time it is?
quests.ruleExplanation: What time it is uses statement word order after do you know, not the inverted what time is it you'd expect standing alone.
quests.nativeTip: Do you know is followed by statement order too, keeping the embedded question from inverting.

quests.sentence: I wonder if she is coming.
quests.ruleExplanation: If she is coming uses statement word order after I wonder, embedding the question inside a statement rather than asking it directly.
quests.nativeTip: I wonder introduces an embedded question with if, again using statement word order.

quests.sentence: He explained that the delay was caused by weather.
quests.ruleExplanation: Explained that the delay was caused introduces a passive, backshifted clause, showing that reporting verbs work with a range of clause types.
quests.nativeTip: Explained introduces a reported statement with that, followed by a full backshifted clause.

quests.sentence: She mentioned that she might be late.
quests.ruleExplanation: Mentioned that she might be late introduces a reported clause using might, a modal that stays the same in reported speech.
quests.nativeTip: Mentioned works the same way as said, introducing a reported clause with that.

quests.sentence: He wondered whether the plan would work.
quests.ruleExplanation: Wondered whether the plan would work introduces an embedded question using whether, similar to the if/whether pattern used with asked.
quests.nativeTip: Wondered introduces an embedded question with whether, just like asked did with if/whether earlier.

quests.sentence: She said that she had already submitted the report.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had already submitted combines the past-perfect backshift with already in its usual mid-position, reviewing two skills together.
quests.nativeTip: Combine the past-perfect backshift with already, reviewing a pattern from Present Perfect and applying it in reported speech.

quests.sentence: He asked if I could help him move the boxes.
quests.ruleExplanation: If I could help him move combines the if-plus-statement-order pattern with the causative structure help him move, reviewing two different files' skills together.
quests.nativeTip: Combine a reported yes/no question with a causative verb pattern (help someone do something).

quests.sentence: They wondered why the flight had been delayed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Why the flight had been delayed combines the reported-WH-question pattern with past perfect passive, layering two of the curriculum's most advanced structures together.
quests.nativeTip: Combine a reported WH question with past perfect passive — two advanced structures in one sentence.
